headline: South Africa and Canada Adjust Trade Ties Amid US Tariff Friction
summary: Rising commercial friction and trade tariffs under US President Donald Trump are driving trade realignments, with South Africa lifting China exports by 25% and Canada announcing a C$142 billion plan.
why: US trade barriers are pushing traditional trade partners to diversify exports and deploy domestic fiscal support to cushion industrial sectors.

impacts.name: South Africa
impacts.why: South Africa expanded exports to China by 25% to navigate escalating commercial friction with the United States.

impacts.why: Canada introduced a C$142 billion economic plan in response to restructuring global trade relationships.
